name: quake3
title: QUAKE III ARENA 1.32 (Linux/GLX, id386=0, interpreted QVMs)
_units: code/unix/Makefile's linuxquake3: Q3OBJ plus the linux Q3POBJ, each object mapped to its source by the Makefile's own rule (135 C files). Left out, each for the build's own reason: snd_mixa.s and matha.s (the i386 assembly; with __i386__ undefined q_shared.h sets id386 0 and the C beside them is compiled), vm_x86.o (added only for ARCH i386), and the thirteen ft2/ objects, whose directory the GPL release does not contain and which tr_font.c uses only under BUILD_FREETYPE, which the Makefile never defines. The C++ splines are commented out of the Makefile itself. One file the Makefile does not list and its own sources need: unix/linux_signals.c, which defines InitSig, called from unix_main.c and linux_glimp.c -- the same staleness as Quake II's linux/Makefile.i386.
_defines: __linux__ is what gcc on Linux predefines and what q_shared.h selects the platform by (PRISM predefines no OS); every test that would pick assembly reads __linux__ && __i386__, so with __i386__ and i386 undefined, as for Quake, the C paths stay in.
_args: vm_game/vm_cgame/vm_ui 1 = interpret the bytecode: without vm_x86.c there is no VM_Compile, and the default (compiled) would call it. The engine's own setting. net_noudp 1 is the engine's own switch for running without an IP socket: this Linux layer has no POSIX sockets here, NET_OpenIP would end in 'Couldn't allocate IP port', and a local game talks to its own server over the loopback anyway. sv_pure 0: a pure server makes its clients load the QVMs COMPILED (cl_ui.c, cl_cgame.c) whatever vm_ui/vm_cgame say, and there is no compiler without vm_x86.c; the local server is made impure, the engine's own setting.
_unitDefines: The Makefile compiles botlib with DO_BOT_CC, which adds -DBOTLIB; everything else with DO_CC. NDEBUG is RELEASE_CFLAGS'. unix_main.c alone gets __i386__ back: it has no assembly, and reads the macro only to name the architecture (the arch cvar, and the qagamei386.so a native game would be, which interpreted QVMs never load); without one it stops at #error Unknown arch.
_compile: longDouble 64 is gcc's -mlong-double-64: botlib's script parser keeps every number in a long double, and PRISM represents the IEEE-double form of it, not the x87 extended one (tools/gate-long-double64.mjs). The reference build is given the same flag.
_asmTranslate: Sys_SnapVector is assembly on Linux i386 -- unix_shared.c compiles its C one only for __APPLE__ -- and the game VMs call it every frame through trap_SnapVector. So the program's own snapvector.nasm is translated (x87: the control word, fld/fistp/fild/fstp) and bound like any function; tools/gate-asm-snapvector.mjs holds the translation to Unicorn running the same file, 300 of 300 vectors.
